oil.summary: Crude benchmarks pulled back modestly on the day — WTI off 0.81% to $82.53, Brent -0.60% to $88.39 — after touching $89 intraday on Hormuz tension headlines, with a bearish API print (surprise 9.072 million barrel build for the week ending Aug 7) and a sharp RBOB sell-off (-8.93%) adding downward pressure on the refined-products complex. The weekly picture remains bullish: Brent +11.24%, WTI +9.72%, supported by the IEA's warning of a 1.8 million bpd global deficit this quarter following a projected 4.3 million bpd supply drop tied to the Strait of Hormuz closure. Indian state refiners are actively tendering for 6 million barrels of spot crude as term flows stay constrained. Tanker data continues to contradict U.S. government claims of normalized Middle East flows, keeping a geopolitical risk premium firmly embedded in the curve.
drivers: IEA projects 1.8 million bpd global deficit this quarter; supply forecast cut by 4.3 million bpd on sustained Hormuz disruption
Bearish API inventory report — 9.072 million barrel surprise crude build — capped the intraday rally and weighed on WTI
RBOB gasoline crashed 8.93% on the day, diverging sharply from crude; heating oil also fell 3.26% despite the broader weekly bullish trend
sources: The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies

gas.summary: Henry Hub edged higher (+1.66% to $2.812/MMBtu) with a modest weekly gain of +4.65%, though the month-on-month picture remains soft at -3.13%, suggesting the domestic market has yet to fully price in geopolitical spillovers. TTF was the standout mover, surging 3.61% on the day to €60.855/MWh, extending a sharp 16.13% weekly rally and a 14.91% monthly gain as the Hormuz crisis tightens European LNG supply alternatives. The Alaska LNG mega-project ($55 billion) is reportedly in active talks with additional buyers ahead of FID, a sign that long-term buyers are scrambling for supply security. Headlines on Russia's refinery crisis and its import of Indian fuels add to the broader supply dislocation narrative. Gas-specific news flow today was relatively thin beyond these items.
drivers: TTF surged 3.61% on the day (+16.13% on the week) as Hormuz disruption tightens European LNG import alternatives
Alaska LNG project advancing buyer talks ahead of FID, reflecting long-term supply security demand from buyers in a disrupted market
Henry Hub gains remain muted relative to TTF; the US-Europe price spread continues to widen, incentivizing LNG export flows

power.summary: EU carbon (EUA) was broadly flat, slipping 0.28% to $77.69, with a mild weekly gain of +0.75% and monthly drift of +1.42% — the carbon market appears to be awaiting clearer direction from the gas complex before moving decisively. The dominant power story today was the UK grid warning of tighter supply margins during a solar eclipse coinciding with a heatwave, creating a rare dual demand-and-supply stress event. TTF's continued surge (+3.61% to €60.855/MWh) raises gas-fired generation costs materially across European power markets. A drone strike on the power station at Libya's Zawiya oil export terminal added to infrastructure risk sentiment. Iran-related geopolitical headlines remain in the background but have not yet catalyzed a directional EUA move.
drivers: UK grid flagged a power margin shortfall risk as a solar eclipse combined with a heatwave stressed supply and demand simultaneously
TTF at €60.855/MWh (+16% on the week) is pushing up gas-fired generation costs across European power markets, with limited EUA response so far
Drone strike on the Zawiya power station in Libya highlights growing vulnerability of energy infrastructure to conflict-zone attacks
